title: Agent Loop Boundary
summary: Defines the AgentLoop turn/session conductor boundary: what it owns, what it delegates, allowed and forbidden dependencies, and how new runtime components are added.

sections.content: AgentLoop (rig_relay/core/agent_loop.py) is the turn/session conductor, not the runtime kernel. It owns conversation topology: start session, start turn, get context, call model, delegate tools, continue or finish, save state, emit lifecycle events. Policy for each subsystem lives outside AgentLoop.

rows: Turn/session topology, public API (act(), fork(), compact(), clear_history())
Mutable session/turn state snapshot. Readiness, stats, limits, session identity
One-turn phase state machine. Phase transitions, outcome, tool batch metadata
Turn phase event recorder, result builder, trace evidence emitter, loop decision policy (Phase 2A)
Provider call preparation, streaming and non-streaming calls, retry/error classification
Tool response recording, telemetry, failure event construction
Message history cleanup, missing response filling, session reset, fork message extraction
Approval callbacks, tool permissions, session rules
Session lifecycle telemetry emission, context observation
Context envelope construction and assembly telemetry
Middleware pipeline setup, result handling, backend metadata
Mission metadata to AgentLoop context/runtime wiring

sections.content: AgentLoop refactor Waves 2-6 extracted 5 standalone runtime modules from the monolith (1806 → 991 lines, 45% reduction). Each owns a coherent responsibility domain and is composed into AgentLoop rather than mixed in via MRO.

rows: Adapter factory, council gating, execution orchestration, concurrency (782 lines)
Fork, compact, clear_history, switch_agent, reload, runtime_state (292 lines)
Permission gating, approval policy, write gating, mutation legality checks (101 lines)
Correlation IDs, OTel spans, lifecycle event emission (85 lines)
Canonical turn result with 11 structured fields (58 lines)

sections.content: These must not be imported by AgentLoop or any mixin in rig_relay/core/:

rows: Desktop is a consumer of projections/intents, not runtime policy
Ralph is an observe-only scanner that consumes projections
Scripts are CLI entry points, not runtime policy
Analytics compiler consumes events/ledgers, must not execute runtime work
Report query is a consumer, not runtime policy
Bash analytics is a consumer, not runtime policy
DuckDB is the analytical compiler substrate. Runtime must not depend on it

sections.content:
Desktop / Ralph / Scripts (outer)
        |
        | consume projections, intents, events
        v
AgentLoop + Runtimes (inner)
        |
        | use
        v
Tools, Config, LLM Backends, Context Compiler (inner)
Inner runtime policy must not know outer mechanisms. Desktop, Ralph, and scripts are outer consumers. They import from core; core never imports from them.

items: Create the module in rig_relay/core/ (e.g. tool_runtime.py)
Add it as a mixin or standalone class depending on coupling
Wire it into AgentLoop through composition or MRO
Add to the runtime components table
Add an architecture test confirming the dependency boundary
Never import desktop, Ralph, scripts, analytics, or DuckDB from the new component

sections.content: A method belongs outside AgentLoop if: it can be tested without constructing a full AgentLoop; changing its subsystem policy requires editing AgentLoop; it spends most of its code using attributes from a single domain. AgentLoop methods that survive extraction should read as coordination and delegate domain work to dedicated runtimes.

items: AgentLoop and mixins must not import desktop/Ralph/scripts/DuckDB/analytics
